entries.title: Looks can restyle the summaries
entries.body: A Look of your own can now draw the stage summary and the match summary its own way. Pick its style under Stage summary or Match summary on the Export page. On the computer app.

entries.title: Suggested movement, and Keep all
entries.body: Breakdown now suggests movement where you moved, before a late first shot too, beside its suggested reloads. Keep all, above the shot list, confirms every suggestion on the stage at once.

entries.title: Overview counts only shooters you filmed
entries.body: On the Overview, a stage's beep, shots and audit counts now leave out shooters with no footage of it, and a stage nobody was filmed on says No footage.

entries.title: Better shot detection, head cameras most
entries.body: Detection now picks a stage's shots together, using the rhythm of real splits and the stage time, so fewer echoes and missed shots, on head cameras most. It applies to stages detected from now on.

entries.title: Change a stage's primary camera safely
entries.body: Setting another clip as Primary on the Footage page keeps the stage's audit as a backup, keeps a beep you confirmed, and detects the shots again on the new camera, asking first.

entries.title: Confirm a beep, then audit and save
entries.body: After confirming a beep in Audit, a quick shot detection could leave the page on the stage as it was before, and Save said the stage was saved elsewhere. Audit now shows the new shots.

entries.title: Link a shooter to the scoreboard later
entries.body: A shooter added by name has no stage times, so Audit cannot trim. Link to scoreboard in their menu on the Footage page picks them on the scoreboard and brings the times in.

entries.title: Sort footage keeps every clip you name
entries.body: On Sort footage, naming a clip from a camera whose clock is unknown no longer undoes the clip you named before it, and a stage picked before the shooter stays picked.

entries.title: A camera that started during the beep
entries.body: On the phone's beep card, Beep starts before the clip puts the line on the tone's end and sets the beep that tone's length earlier, measured on the stage's head cams.

entries.title: A quiet beep you can see and land on
entries.body: The beep picker, on the phone and in Audit's beep step, draws what is on screen at full height. On the phone the line lands on the beep's start; Snap is beside the zoom buttons.

entries.title: Recheck every secondary camera's beep
entries.body: Recheck secondary beeps, in the Audit menu on the desktop or the phone, walks each extra camera's beep in the match. Move one and confirm, or Looks right to go on.

entries.title: Seat all stays on the stage you are on
entries.body: After seating shots on one stage, Seat all on the next stage on the desktop could move shots seconds away, onto another stage's times. It now seats each shot where it sits on this stage.

entries.title: Audit never draws half a stage
entries.body: When a stage's audio is not ready yet, Audit, beep review and the take waveform say Preparing audio and load it as soon as it is, instead of drawing a stage that ends early.

entries.title: The waveform stays under its markers
entries.body: Zoomed in and scrolled to the end of a stage, the waveform could slide a few pixels ahead of the shot markers. It now stays lined up at every zoom.

entries.title: Step a shot back to the blast
entries.body: When Seat puts a shot on the louder echo after it, Earlier on the phone or Shift+E on the desktop moves it to the burst before. Hold P or Q to peek at rejected shots.

entries.title: Place the beep exactly on its start
entries.body: Beep review draws the beep in full detail when you zoom in, says when the beep sits 20 ms or more from the tone's start, and Snap to the beep's start moves it there.

entries.title: The waveform covers the whole stage again
entries.body: On some stages the Audit waveform ended before the audio did, so the playhead ran off the last row. The waveform is now always drawn from the stage audio you hear.

entries.title: The zoomed view sits on top on the phone
entries.body: On the phone's Audit page the zoomed view and its zoom buttons are above the whole-stage waveform, so your thumb never covers it while you scrub.

entries.title: Save and next on the phone
entries.body: On the phone's Audit page, Save & next saves and opens the next stage or shooter. Tap the title to pick any shooter and stage, and Back returns to where you came from.

entries.title: A steadier phone Audit
entries.body: On the phone's Audit page a tap moves the playhead without playing, a drag can go up or down rows, the page no longer jumps, and the loop follows the shot you pick.

entries.title: Seat shots on their rise foot on the phone
entries.body: On the phone's Audit page, Seat puts the selected shot on its rise foot and an added shot lands there. Seat all and the Snap switch are in the stage menu.

entries.title: Synced videos play on splitsmith.app
entries.body: Some synced matches showed no video on splitsmith.app. The desktop now checks every clip it has cut and cuts a broken or missing one again on the next sync.

entries.title: Place shots on their rise foot in Audit
entries.body: Placed shots snap to the rise foot at any zoom; hold Shift to place exactly, or turn Snap off in the timeline's menu. E seats the current shot, and the menu can seat them all.

entries.title: Videos show their first frame in Safari
entries.body: In Safari a stage's main video stayed black under Loading video until you pressed Play. It now shows its first frame as soon as it loads, as in other browsers.

entries.title: Big syncs finish on a slow connection
entries.body: The first sync of a match with many clips could stop with a timeout on a home connection and fail again on every retry. Uploads now wait long enough for each part.

entries.title: Phone Audit draws shots on their sounds
entries.body: On the phone's Audit page the whole-stage waveform drifted a little further from its shot marks on every row, up to 0.4 s on the last. Each sound now sits under its marks.

entries.title: The video follows a dragged region edge
entries.body: In Breakdown, dragging a region's edge now scrubs the video under the pointer while the edge still snaps to a shot. Snap to shots can be turned off in the timeline's options menu.

entries.title: Nudging a region shows the frame
entries.body: In Breakdown, moving a region's start or end with the arrow keys now takes the video to that frame and shows its time, as dragging the edge does.

entries.title: Logos stay sharp and clear of text
entries.body: A small logo is drawn at its own size. On tall cards logos make room for each other, names take two lines and text stays clear of the app's buttons; summaries keep names clear of logos.

entries.title: Overlay on time when a clip starts late
entries.body: When a video starts only a few seconds before the beep, the overlay's clock and shot count ran late. They now land on the shots, and such a stage's overlay is drawn again on its next export.

entries.title: Older matches redraw their overlay once
entries.body: Export an older match again and its overlay is drawn fresh once, in your Look's current colours and fonts. Its cards and summaries may now carry the shooter's current look and logos.

entries.title: Shot count and clock apart on tall grids
entries.body: In an upright compare video, each tile's shot count could run into its clock. On narrow tiles they now shrink, or the count moves under the clock.

entries.title: Summaries and overlays for upright video
entries.body: On a tall export, summaries, comparison grids included, show splits first and fill the frame, and they and every overlay style keep clear of the captions and buttons Shorts and Reels draw on top.

entries.title: Readable splits on tall grids
entries.body: In a compare video with many shooters on an upright canvas, the stage summary ran each tile's Best, Avg, Worst and Draw into each other. They now stack two to a line.

entries.title: Shot video opens at the shot on a phone
entries.body: On a phone, Video in Audit now opens 1.5 s before the shot you tapped and stops the shot's sound. It used to start at the beginning or at a later shot.

entries.title: Other cameras in a corner of the video
entries.body: In Splits, Audit, Coach and Breakdown the other cameras play in a corner of the video; click it or press C to swap. On a phone, Audit's Video stacks them: tap one for its controls.

entries.title: Audit controls on the timeline
entries.body: On Audit, play, loop, the shot filter and the marker key now sit on the timeline's top row, and its ... menu holds the rest, so more of the waveform fits on a laptop screen.

entries.title: Moved shots stay where you put them
entries.body: A shot you moved on Audit came back at the detector's time the next time you opened the stage, and saving again undid your move. It now stays where you placed it.

entries.title: Match summary fits vertical video
entries.body: On a vertical or square video, the match summary (Look on the Export page) now keeps every figure and the match name on the card.

entries.title: Review a stage on Coach
entries.body: Coach now shows the stage video, a strip of its shots and reloads, the figures, and notes on the stage and each shot that save as you type. To change regions or intervals, use Adjust in Breakdown.

entries.title: Mark movement and reloads on a stage
entries.body: Open Breakdown in the Analyse group of a match to mark movement, reloads and activations on the timeline and set each shot's interval, with the video beside it. Works on a computer.

entries.title: Place shots to the millisecond
entries.body: Zoom the Audit waveform until each shot's rising edge shows and drop a marker right on it. Zoomed out, a dropped marker snaps to the start of the shot; hold Shift to place it exactly.

entries.title: Better shot detection on Meta glasses footage
entries.body: Shot detection now finds far more shots in footage from recent Meta Vanguard glasses, including stages without a round count. It applies to stages detected from now on.

entries.title: A full-width, zoomable timeline
entries.body: Breakdown's lanes, Audit's waveform and beep confirmation now share one full-width timeline. Zoom up to 16x, and turn on wheel zoom from the timeline's menu next to Follow playhead.

entries.title: The stage list keeps you where you are
entries.body: Picking a stage in the left bar on Coach, Splits, Export or Compare now opens that stage there, for the shooter you are looking at, instead of always going to Audit.

entries.title: A closing card made for YouTube end screens
entries.body: Pick the End screen style for the closing card under Look on the Export page. It holds 10 seconds and leaves the right side free for YouTube's subscribe and next video elements.

entries.title: Logos that make a video look finished
entries.body: Your brand rides the wipe between stages, the shooter's logo sits on the summaries and the YouTube thumbnail is a designed card. Choose under Logos in Details on the Export page.

entries.title: A Shooters page and your account menu
entries.body: Set each shooter's logo, colour and club once on the new Shooters page, from the account menu at the top right. Every match follows, and a shooter chip in a match opens it too.

entries.title: See where each logo goes
entries.body: The Export preview and the Look editor mark every logo spot with a dashed square until a logo is set: the shooter's, your brand and the event's. Turn it off with Show where logos go.

entries.title: Copied Looks keep up with new card features
entries.body: A Look you duplicate now draws the current cards, so it gets new features like your brand logo. An older copy shows a note beside the preview on the Export page with a button to catch up.

entries.title: Clearer saving in Audit
entries.body: Finishing the audit takes you to Splits, and if a stage was saved elsewhere while you edited, Audit asks whether to keep your edits or load the saved version instead of dropping them.

entries.title: See where the timer stopped in Audit
entries.body: A dotted line on the Audit waveform marks the scorecard's stage time, and a flag names the shots after it or a missed last shot, so the video's clock matches the stage time.

entries.title: Overlay styles with motion
entries.body: Pick Plate, Pips, Ticker, Timeline or Minimal under Overlay in Look on the Export page: the clock, shot count and splits animate on every shot and land on the stage time.

entries.title: Your brand and your shooter book
entries.body: Set your brand once on the new You page and it marks every video you render. A shooter's colour, club and logo now follow them from match to match.

entries.title: A match summary at the end of the video
entries.body: Turn on Match summary under Look on the Export page: after the last stage, your average split, best draw, hits and a row per stage. On the grid, each shooter gets a tile.

entries.title: Made with splitsmith on the closing card
entries.body: The closing card now ends with a small Made with splitsmith line. Turn it off under Credit in Details on the Export page; your choice is kept with your presets.

entries.title: The event's logo on the title page
entries.body: Add the match's own logo under Branding in Details on the Export page. The title page and closing card show it above the match name.

entries.title: Your brand on the title page
entries.body: Add your club, personal or sponsor logo and a line to a Look under Card styles, Your brand. The title page and closing card show it in the top left corner.

entries.title: Club line from the scoreboard
entries.body: Linking a shooter to their scoreboard entry now fills their club line for the cards, unless you already typed one.

entries.title: Make your own Look
entries.body: Pick Make your own beside the Looks on the Export page, name it and choose what it starts from. Discard removes a new Look you changed your mind about.

entries.title: A clearer Look editor
entries.body: The preview now says when it is updating and shows a still before the animation, colours have plain names, and a demo scene lets you compare Looks without footage.

entries.title: Look previews on synced matches
entries.body: On splitsmith.app, the Look editor and the Export preview now draw the cards of a match synced from the desktop app instead of staying blank.

entries.title: Your own font in a Look
entries.body: Add a TTF or OTF file under Card styles, Fonts in the Look editor and use it for titles or figures, the clock included. Desktop app only.

entries.title: Faster second renders of a compare grid
entries.body: Rendering a compare grid again reuses every stage, card and transition that did not change, as a single shooter's video already did.

entries.title: Club colours on Compare and shared pages
entries.body: A shooter's accent and logo now mark them on Compare, in the shooter chips and on the Splits pages, shared links included.

entries.title: Previews that move
entries.body: An animated card or sting now plays in the Export page's preview and in the Look editor, looping, on your own footage.

entries.title: Broken templates show before you export
entries.body: When your own Look has a template that fails, the Export page says which cards would be left out before you render, with the line that broke.

entries.title: Choose your Look's fonts
entries.body: Pick the title and figure faces under Card styles in the Look editor; the cards, the stage summary and the running clock all draw with them.

entries.title: Long stage names fit the cards
entries.body: A long stage name on the title page, a slate or the lower third shrinks to fit the frame, and ends in an ellipsis when it still does not.

entries.title: Palettes that stand out on your footage
entries.body: The Look editor suggests full palettes from one colour, from your club logo, from ready-made range palettes, or from what stands out on this match's own footage.

entries.title: Write your own card templates
entries.body: In the desktop app, the Look editor's Templates tab edits a card's HTML with a live preview, the data it receives and a check that names the broken line.

entries.title: Make your own Look
entries.body: Duplicate a Look under Look, Advanced on the Export page, pick its colours and card styles, and see it on your own footage before you save.

entries.title: Transitions between stages
entries.body: An MP4 can cross from one stage to the next with a fade, a wipe or a dozen other moves, each with a direction. The compare grid gets them too.

entries.title: Stings in your colours
entries.body: A sting sweeps a band in your Look's colours across the cut between stages, carrying the club logo when there is one. Pick Wipe sting under transitions.

entries.title: Cards that rise into place
entries.body: Choose the Rise style for the title page, the stage slates, the lower third or the closing card, and their lines animate in.

entries.title: Your club colour and logo
entries.body: Give each shooter an accent colour, a club line and a logo on the Footage page. The cards, the sting and the stage summary use them.

entries.title: A better beep finder
entries.body: The first beep suggested for a stage is now the right one far more often, so there is less to confirm by hand.

entries.title: Smoother scrubbing in Audit
entries.body: Audit plays a lighter 720p copy of each trim, so seeking stays quick on long 4K clips.

entries.title: Clips you already imported
entries.body: Adding a clip again, even from another folder, is recognised and skipped, and the import says why it skipped each file.

entries.title: Your division on the title page
entries.body: The title page prints the shooter's division as the scoreboard has it. Turn it off under Details on the Export page.
